claim.why_it_matters: The diagram is restructured lossily: the callout labels "Data items" and "Methods" are interleaved into the member lists (reading as if "Methods" were a method name), the CheckingAccount method calculateCharges is detached below the table instead of sitting in the CheckingAccount box, and the inheritance arrows are lost. Informative annex E; the prose below restates the members.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page 774 (PDF p796) shows Figure E.7 as described: an Account box with a data compartment (account-number, balance, date-opened) and a methods compartment (deposit, withdraw, balance), external callouts 'Data items' and 'Methods' with arrows to those compartments, and two subclass boxes, CheckingAccount (charges / displayCharges, calculateCharges) and SavingAccount (interest-rate / calculateInterest), each with an arrow up to Account. The transcription puts the 'Data items' label on the same line as 'balance' and puts 'Methods' as a line between 'deposit' and 'withdraw', so it reads like a member. It also moves calculateCharges out of the CheckingAccount table column into a stray paragraph and drops the inheritance arrows. All the words survive, but the figure's structure (which member belongs to which class, and the subclass relation) is garbled. That is a genuine but informative-only discrepancy: annex E is informative, and the prose that follows restates every member and the inheritance. The quotes are accurate, except that markdown_says leaves out the 'Account' heading line, which the transcription does carry.
verdict.corrected_description: Figure E.7 (informative annex E) is transcribed lossily. The callouts 'Data items' and 'Methods' are interleaved into the Account member lists, calculateCharges is detached from the CheckingAccount column, and the inheritance arrows from CheckingAccount and SavingAccount up to Account are lost. The 'Account' heading is present. No normative content is affected, and the following prose restates the members and the inheritance.
